title: AWS Continuum's sandbox exploit-validation goes industry baseline by H1 2027
body: AWS unveiled Continuum at its New York Summit as an AI-native, model-agnostic vulnerability-management service whose defining move is validation by construction: rather than ranking findings by a static CVSS score, it builds a working exploit in a sandbox to prove a finding is genuinely reachable and exploitable before it ever reaches a human, filtering false positives and prioritizing by real production and business impact. This prediction holds that exploit-validation-as-a-stage stops being one hyperscaler's differentiator and becomes the expected baseline for AI-driven application-security tooling: by the first half of 2027 at least three additional named vendors or platforms in the AI code-security and ASPM space (for example incumbent SAST/ASPM vendors, an autonomous-pentest startup, or a rival cloud) will ship or document a feature that automatically constructs and runs a sandboxed proof-of-exploit to confirm a finding before surfacing it, rather than only scoring or de-duplicating alerts. The driver is the alert-fatigue economics that Continuum is explicitly built to attack: security teams drowning in unreachable, unexploitable findings will not pay for yet another scanner that adds noise, so the competitive frontier shifts from how many issues a tool finds to how few false alarms it forwards, and machine-built proof-of-exploit is the cheapest credible way to make that guarantee. The autonomous-pentesting tooling already visible at adjacent venues, such as the live offensive-security agent demos on this week's calendar, supplies the technical substrate that makes broad adoption plausible within the window.

summary: AWS Continuum, launched at the NYC Summit, validates a code vulnerability by building a working sandbox exploit before surfacing it, killing false positives. By H1 2027 at least three more named AI security vendors should ship automated sandbox exploit-validation, making proof-of-exploit a baseline.
